public_findings.title: [ANN][MAJ] Majolica | RandomX PoW | CPU-Mineable | Fixed Before Block Zero
public_findings.snippet: About Built to a fixed recipe, fired once. Majolica (MAJ) is a proof-of-work network running RandomX on ordinary processors. The name comes from tin-glazed pottery: the painter completes the whole picture while the surface is still raw, and the kiln then simply preserves it - nothing can be retouched afterwards. The same order governs this network. The cap, the block cadence, the stage-1 reward, the halving rhythm and the difficulty rule were written into public source code and published before block zero existed, so nothing was tuned after launch, because there was no launch decision left to make. public_findings.title: [ANN] ReSatoshi | Bitcoin Core + 100-Year UTXO Recycling | No Premine
public_findings.snippet: ReSatoshi ReSatoshi is an independent SHA-256d Proof-of-Work blockchain based on Bitcoin Core 31.0, with selected fixes backported from Bitcoin Core 31.1. ReSatoshi is not affiliated with Satoshi Nakamoto, Bitcoin, or the Bitcoin Core project. The code is kept as close to upstream Bitcoin Core as practical. Beyond the changes required for an independent network, ReSatoshi adds three connected consensus rules: A spendable UTXO expires 5,256,000 blocks after its creationapproximately 100 years at the 10-minute target interval.
